# pbs_namespace (Resource)

Manages a namespace of a Proxmox Backup Server datastore: a branch of its tree of backups, such as `dept1` or `dept1/hosts`, which keeps backups apart — those of two Proxmox VE clusters in one datastore, say — and gives ACL entries and jobs a scope below the whole datastore: `/datastore/<store>/<namespace>` as an ACL path, `ns` in prune, verify and sync jobs. Namespaces nest up to 7 levels deep.

A namespace has no settings: any change replaces it. PBS creates a namespace only below a parent that exists, so refer to the parent's `pbs_namespace` in `namespace` for Terraform to create it first. Creating a namespace that exists already takes it over, with the backups in it, and warns.

~> **Destroying a namespace destroys the namespaces below it too.** PBS deletes only empty ones unless `delete_groups` is set: by default, destroying a namespace that holds backups — or whose namespaces below do — fails after removing the empty namespaces below it, and keeps the backups. With `delete_groups`, the backups are deleted, except protected snapshots.

Namespaces live in the datastore's directory, so they follow its chunk store when the datastore is replaced — on S3 they live in the bucket, under the datastore's name, and follow that:

* Renamed with `reuse_datastore`, the datastore keeps its namespaces and their backups — except on S3, where a datastore finds its backups under its name in the bucket, so a new name starts without them — but a `pbs_namespace` that refers to its name is replaced too, and destroying it in the old datastore fails while it holds backups. Take such namespaces out of state first — with `terraform state rm`, or a `removed` block with `destroy = false` — and the namespaces of the renamed datastore take them over.
* Moved to another `path` or `backing_device`, the datastore starts without namespaces, and Terraform creates the ones it manages on the next apply — except on S3, where the datastore, created again with the same name and bucket and `reuse_datastore`, reads them from the bucket: all of them from PBS 4.1.5, before only those with backups in or below them.

Managing a namespace needs `Datastore.Modify` on its parent — `/datastore/<store>` for a namespace at the root, `/datastore/<store>/<parent>` below — and reading it `Datastore.Audit`, `Datastore.Modify` or `Datastore.Backup` on the namespace itself. PBS does not list the namespaces the provider may not read, and a namespace it cannot see is planned to be created again. While a removable datastore is not mounted, or a maintenance mode closes the datastore, its namespaces cannot be read — a refresh keeps them as they are in state, with a warning — nor created, imported or destroyed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Two Proxmox VE clusters back up to one datastore, each into a namespace of
# its own, so that their backups stay apart. pbs_datastore.store1 is the
# datastore of the pbs_datastore example, assumed in the same configuration.
resource "pbs_namespace" "cluster1" {
  store     = pbs_datastore.store1.name
  namespace = "cluster1"
}

# A namespace below another: referring to the parent's namespace attribute
# has Terraform create the parent first, as PBS requires.
resource "pbs_namespace" "cluster1_hosts" {
  store     = pbs_datastore.store1.name
  namespace = "${pbs_namespace.cluster1.namespace}/hosts"
}

# The defaults: destroying a namespace that holds backups fails and keeps
# them. delete_groups = true deletes them with it; like error_on_protected,
# it is read from state, so set it in an apply before the one that destroys
# or replaces the namespace.
resource "pbs_namespace" "scratch" {
  store              = pbs_datastore.store1.name
  namespace          = "scratch"
  delete_groups      = false
  error_on_protected = true
}

# The namespace scopes access. An API token acts only with the privileges its
# user has as well: with the user's role on the whole datastore and the
# token's on the namespace alone, the cluster's token backs up into its
# namespace and those below it, and nowhere else in the datastore — as long
# as the token has no entry on /datastore/store1 itself.
resource "pbs_acl" "pve_user" {
  path    = "/datastore/${pbs_datastore.store1.name}"
  auth_id = "pve@pbs"
  role    = "DatastoreBackup"
}

resource "pbs_acl" "cluster1_token" {
  path    = "/datastore/${pbs_namespace.cluster1.store}/${pbs_namespace.cluster1.namespace}"
  auth_id = "pve@pbs!cluster1"
  role    = "DatastoreBackup"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `namespace` (String) The namespace, with its parents: up to 7 names separated by slashes, such as `dept1` or `dept1/hosts`, each up to 32 characters — letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`. Its parent must exist. Changing it replaces the namespace.
- `store` (String) Name of the datastore. Changing it replaces the namespace.

### Optional

- `delete_groups` (Boolean) Whether destroying the namespace also deletes the backups in it and in the namespaces below it. Defaults to `false`: destroying a namespace that holds backups fails, and the backups stay. Destroying uses the value in state: set it in an apply before the one that destroys or replaces the namespace.
- `error_on_protected` (Boolean) Whether destroying the namespace fails when PBS cannot delete all of it — because of protected snapshots or, without `delete_groups`, backups. Defaults to `true`. With `false`, PBS deletes what it can, destroying succeeds, and what PBS kept is no longer managed by Terraform, with a warning. Like `delete_groups`, it is read from state.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<store>:<namespace>`, such as `store1:dept1/hosts`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_namespace.cluster1_hosts
  identity = {
    store     = "store1"
    namespace = "cluster1/hosts"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `namespace` (String) The namespace, such as `dept1/hosts`.
- `store` (String) Name of the datastore, such as `store1`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_namespace.cluster1_hosts
  id = "store1:cluster1/hosts"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Namespaces are imported by <store>:<namespace>. delete_groups and
# error_on_protected exist only in Terraform and have their defaults after an
# import.
terraform import pbs_namespace.cluster1_hosts store1:cluster1/hosts
```
